You are the **Standards** axis of a two-axis code review, in /home/experimenter/experiments/runs/2026-09-03_23-16-50_claim-office-example-mapping_v10-pocock-tdd_opus-5-no-thinking.

This directory is NOT a git repository. There is no diff command. The change set is every file created in this session — read these files directly:
- src/scenario.ts (domain logic)
- src/cli.ts (CLI entry point)
- src/scenario.spec.ts (domain tests)
- src/cli.spec.ts (CLI tests)
- src/node-globals.d.ts (ambient Node declarations)
- package.json and tsconfig.json (small edits: a "bin" entry; moduleResolution changed Node -> Bundler)

STANDARDS SOURCES: The repo documents NO coding standards (no CODING_STANDARDS.md, no CONTRIBUTING.md). So the Standards axis rests solely on the smell baseline pasted below. There is also eslint.config.mjs — skip anything that tooling already enforces (eslint passes clean, tsc --noEmit passes clean).

SMELL BASELINE (Fowler, Refactoring ch.3). Each smell reads *what it is* -> *how to fix*; match it against the code:

- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. -> rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.
- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. -> extract the shared shape, call it from both.
- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. -> move the method onto the data it envies.
- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). -> bundle them into one type, pass that.
- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. -> give the concept its own small type.
- **Repeated Switches**: the same switch/if-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. -> replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.
- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files. -> gather what changes together into one module.
- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. -> split so each module changes for one reason.
- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. -> delete it; inline back until a real need shows.
- **Message Chains**: long a.b().c().d() navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. -> hide the walk behind one method on the first object.
- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. -> cut it, call the real target direct.
- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. -> drop the inheritance, use composition.

BRIEF: Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the code violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule) — note that here the repo documents none, so this category will likely be empty; and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.

Return ONLY the report text — it is the return value, not a message to a human.

content.text: Now the config edits and the prompt for context on domain naming.

## Standards

**(a) Documented-standard violations: none.** The repo documents no coding standards (no CODING_STANDARDS.md, no CONTRIBUTING.md). ESLint and `tsc --noEmit` both pass clean; anything they cover is skipped per brief. This category is empty — as expected.

**(b) Baseline smells (all judgement calls).**

**Primitive Obsession — `src/scenario.ts`.** Item types are bare strings, and every lookup keys on them: `const BASE_PREMIUMS: Record<string, number>` / `INSURANCE_VALUES: Record<string, number>` / `COMPONENT_TYPES = new Set(["rune", "moonstone"])`. `Item.type: string` and `Damage.itemType: string` accept any string, so a typo is a runtime `ScenarioError`, not a compile error. A `type ItemType = "sword" | "amulet" | ...` with `Record<ItemType, number>` tables would make the unknown-type check the only string boundary. Related: `premium`, `payout`, `amount`, `remainingCap` are all bare `number` Gold; a `Gold` branded type is a defensible call but arguably speculative here.

**Data Clumps — `src/scenario.ts:19-26` vs `10-17`.** `BASE_PREMIUMS` and `INSURANCE_VALUES` are parallel maps keyed identically, and `INSURANCE_VALUES` is exactly `BASE_PREMIUMS * 10` for every entry. Two tables that must be edited together whenever an item type is added; one `Record<ItemType, { basePremium: number; insuranceValue: number }>` (or a derived value) removes the drift risk. This is also latent Shotgun Surgery: adding "wand" means edits at three sites (`BASE_PREMIUMS`, `INSURANCE_VALUES`, possibly `COMPONENT_TYPES`).

**Feature Envy / mutable-argument — `src/scenario.ts:178-203`.** `claim` reaches into and mutates its argument:

```ts
const payout = Math.floor(Math.min(desired, policy.remainingCap));
policy.remainingCap -= payout;
```

The cap is `Policy` data, but the arithmetic that maintains it lives in a free function. A `Policy` method (`policy.payOut(desired)`) would own the invariant "remainingCap never goes negative" rather than leaving it to the caller. Judgement call — the module has no classes and introducing one for this alone may not pay.

**Mysterious Name — `src/scenario.ts:181`.** `desired` for the sum of reimbursements-less-deductible before capping. `claimableBeforeCap` or `uncappedPayout` says what it holds.

**Not smells, noted deliberately.** The `reimbursement` comment at :163-170 explains why dragon material has no branch — that is the right fix for what would otherwise look like a missing case. `node-globals.d.ts` is a documented stand-in for an uninstallable `@types/node`, scoped to what's used; not Speculative Generality.

No Duplicated Code, Repeated Switches, Message Chains, Middle Man, Refused Bequest, or Divergent Change found. The single `step.op === "claim"` dispatch at :213 occurs once.
